title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 223
paragraphs: Xerxes, meanwhile, having made libations at sunrise, waited for some time — until about the hour when the marketplace fills — and then advanced on them. This had been instructed by Epialtes, since the descent of the mountain is shorter, and the distance to cover much less, than the roundabout ascent. So the barbarians under Xerxes were advancing to the attack; and the Greeks under Leonidas, feeling they were going out to meet death, now pushed out much further than before into the broader part of the defile. When the wall's fence was being guarded, they had on the previous days fought retreating before the enemy into the narrow part of the pass; but now they engaged them outside the narrows, and very many of the barbarians fell. For behind them, the divisional leaders with whips in their hands struck every man, driving them ever forward. Many were forced into the sea and perished, and many more still were trodden down alive by one another; and there was no keeping count of the number who died. For, knowing the death about to come upon them because of those going around the mountain, the Greeks displayed against the barbarians the whole extent of their strength — disregarding danger and acting as though possessed by a spirit of recklessness.
